entities.summary: Angelo Sala was an Italian doctor and early iatrochemist. He promoted chemical remedies and, drawing on the relative merits of the conflicting chemical and Galenical systems of medicine, dismissed alchemical transmutation and 'universal medicine'; objected to tartar which had deliquesced being called an 'oil'; observed that metals reacted differently with acids; that sulphur extracted something from the air in order to burn; that silver nitrate darkened on exposure to light; surmised the existence of elementary (atomic) particles; and described newly discovered compounds and methods of preparation.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Angelo Sala's work on chemical remedies and his dismissal of alchemical transmutation contributed to the development of modern chemistry. His observations on metal reactions with acids laid groundwork for later scientists.
